name: Zion Park 1-Day Tour
positioning: Explore Zion National Park during a day trip filled with adventures for outdoor enthusiasts. Book a guided tour, including transportation, food, and entrance.
overview: Photographers and Outdoor enthusiasts alike will enjoy this 12 Hour tour of Zion. With a comfortable small group format, you will have the opportunity to visit many parts of Zion and even have time to walk and hike on some of the trails in the park.
itinerary_raw: Day 1: Zion National Park As you near Zion, you will begin to witness a few of the distinctive landscapes found in this unique geological landscape. Towering mountains and volcanic cinder cones overshadow the distinct red sandstone cliffs that cover this landscape. Lava flows cap the sandstone ridges and provide a unique contrast against the brilliant flaming colors that greet your eyes at every turn. As you enter the park, you will be surrounded by towering cliffs reaching over 3000+ ft (1000+ m) into the air. These are the tallest sandstone cliffs in the world. As you explore the park, you will continue to be in awe of the full colors and grandeur of these cliffs. Flaming reds, brilliant whites, and subtle yellows accented by water stains and desert varnish. These hues are ever-changing throughout the day as the sun and clouds highlight and diminish each other's prominence and stature before your eyes. There will be hiking opportunities on several of Zion's famous trails. This includes Emerald Pools, Weeping Wall, The Narrows (Temple of Sinawava and the Riverwalk trail), Canyon Overlook, Scouts Lookout on Angels Landing, or the beginner Pa'rus Trail. For the photographers, you will have the opportunity to explore the park and capture it from its many viewpoints below and above the canyon rim. For those wanting to just relax and see the beauties of nature, you will have plenty of opportunities to sit and listen to the sounds of nature and watch it continue to evolve around you under the shade of the many cottonwood trees that cover the canyon landscape. A box lunch will be provided to enable you to explore as much of the park as possible. There are many picnic areas within the canyon, or you can enjoy eating while trekking along the trails. Water and snacks, including fruits, will be available as we travel to and from the park. Your guide will provide you with facts and information about the history of the park, its geology, plant science, and a few of the animals that call Zion home. Lunch Included. As you return home at the end of the day, you will be able to relax and discuss your adventures in your comfortable chairs in our tour vehicles. You will be dropped off at your hotel between 6:00 and 6:30 pm in the evening.

name: AMA Paris & Normandy River Cruise
positioning: Discover Paris and Normandy: from Monet’s Gardens and charming Honfleur to D-Day beaches, royal châteaux, art, cuisine, and timeless French beauty.
overview: April 8, 2027 - April 15 2027 Sail roundtrip from Paris on an unforgettable journey along the Seine, where timeless romance meets history and art. Begin in the City of Light before venturing into the heart of Normandy, where dramatic coastlines, charming harbor towns, and world-renowned cuisine await. Each day offers a new perspective—whether strolling through medieval streets, admiring grand châteaux, or sipping regional cider beneath the apple orchards. Step into history as you walk the hallowed grounds of the Normandy beaches, where Allied forces landed during WWII’s D-Day invasion. Discover the legacy of Joan of Arc in Rouen, and immerse yourself in the spirit of the Impressionists in Honfleur and Monet’s Gardens at Giverny. From the “Versailles of Normandy,” Château de Bizy, to the serene landscapes that inspired great artists, every stop blends culture, memory, and beauty. Onboard, your luxury ship is a sanctuary of comfort and style. Savor regionally inspired cuisine with unlimited fine wine and beer, enjoy wellness activities or a dip in the sun-deck pool, and relax with nightly entertainment. With guided tours for every interest—whether gentle walks, active hikes, or cycling through the countryside—you’ll experience France your way. This 7-night cruise is more than a vacation; it’s an immersion into the art, history, and joie de vivre of Northern France.
itinerary_raw: Day 1: ARRIVE IN PARIS Arrive in Paris Board the ship in Paris for you Paris & Normandy Cruise Meals: D Day 2: LES ANDELYS Uncover the history of Château Gaillard, the former stronghold of Richard the Lionheart, situated on the chalk cliffs high above the Seine, on a morning tour. Or, if you prefer a more active adventure, you can hike there from the banks of the Seine, admiring the scenic views along the way. For those who wish to explore the area on two wheels, join a guided bike tour through the charming town of Les Andelys. After your adventures, set sail along the meandering Seine for a scenic cruise. Meals: B, L, D Day 3: LE HAVRE During your time in Le Havre, set out on an excursion to the seaside town of Honfleur, renowned for its picturesque harbor, and for being an inspirational site for Impressionist painters. During the afternoon, you can join a city tour of the UNESCO-designated Le Havre. Alternatively, you have the choice of a bike tour through Le Havre. Meals: B,L,D Day 4: LE HAVRE - NORMANDY BEACHES - CAUDEBEC EN CAUX Experience the Normandy region with a variety of excursions. For those wishing to go to the American sector of the historic Normandy Beaches, you will visit the cemetery at Colleville-sur-Mer, Omaha Beach, the artillery battery at Longues-sur-Mer and the village of Arromanches, where the remains of the floating harbor used during the WWII landings can be seen. If you prefer, you can tour the Gold and Juno beaches in the British and Canadian sectors, where you will visit Ranville Cemetery, Pegasus Bridge, the Canadian cemetery at Beny-sur-Mer, the WWII museum in Courseulle and, finally, Arromanches. Alternatively, you can set out on a full day excursion to the delicious Pays d’Auge region of Normandy, where apple cider, Calvados and pommeau outrank French wine. If you wish to experience a different kind of inspiration in Caudebec-en-Caux, you can journey back in time with the interactive exhibits and vessels at the Seine Museum. Meals: B, L, D Day 5: ROUEN Spend the morning enjoying medieval Rouen with a choice of several excursions. Join a walking tour and see the square where Joan of Arc was martyred, as well as the Medieval Quarter and Great Clock. You also have the choice to go on the “Tastes of Normandy” tour, where you’ll be treated to the delicious flavors of the region, including chocolate, Norman cheese and cider; or get active by going on a guided bike tour. Then visit Bonnemare Castle, a 16th-century architectural treasure lined with picturesque poplar trees. Meals: B, L, D Day 6: VERNON Enjoy scenic cruising around Vernon before disembarking the ship for your excursion. You will have a choice of three excursions, depending on your interests. Visit Claude Monet’s home and gardens in Giverny. Art lovers will immediately recognize images immortalized in Monet’s most beloved paintings—such as water lilies, Japanese bridges and graceful willow trees. Wander around his famous gardens and home where he lived for more than four decades. Or visit the regal 18th-century Château de Bizy, inspired by the opulence of Versailles. Enjoy an escorted tour of the palace and gardens. If you prefer a more active adventure, go on a guided bike tour, taking in the beautiful French countryside. *PLEASE NOTE: Monet's Gardens may be closed; therefore, an alternative tour will operate instead. Meals: B, L, D Day 7: PARIS Travel to Auberge Ravoux in the heart of Auvers-sur-Oise, the last home of artist Vincent van Gogh. His spirit still lingers in his former attic rooms at the Ravoux Inn. The mere 70 days Van Gogh spent in Auvers-sur-Oise were astonishingly prolific as he painted more than 70 works here before his death. Or enjoy the exquisite architecture of the Château de Malmaison, the former home of Napoleon and Josephine Bonaparte, also known as "the most beautiful and curious garden in Europe." Active travelers may instead choose to pedal through Paris from the seat of their bike on a guided cycling tour. In the afternoon, experience the “City of Light” from a unique perspective when you board a modern river boat at the Port de la Bourdonnais, located on the banks of the Seine River near the Eiffel Tower. With exterior seating and viewing platforms, your one-hour cruise will be a dream come true as you glide along the river and underneath Paris’s ornate bridges. From the boat, you will take in panoramic views of the city’s iconic buildings and monuments, including the Musee d’Orsay and the Notre Dame Cathedral. Meals: B, L, D Day 8: DEPART PARIS Bid farewell to Paris and prepare for your flight home Meals: B SPACIOUS STATEROOMS 7 nights luxury accommodation in an outside stateroom (most with twin balconies) Entertainment-On-Demand in all staterooms featuring free high-speed internet access, movies, a music library and English language TV stations Mini-fridge, desk and sitting area Bottled water replenished daily AN ARRAY OF AMENITIES Wellness Activities with a dedicated Wellness Host leading various exercise classes Personalized service from a highly trained Cruise Manager during both cruise and land packages Internet and Wi-Fi access Sun-deck pool with swim-up bar and walking track Fitness room Main Lounge with panoramic views and bar Bottled water in every stateroom replenished daily Daily entertainment including cultural performances AWARD-WINNING DINING All onboard dining in a variety of venues Regionally inspired cuisine made with locally sourced ingredients The Chef’s Table specialty restaurant Welcome Cocktail, Welcome Dinner, La Chaîne des Rôtisseurs Dinner, Captain's Cocktail and Gala Dinner La Chaîne des Rôtisseurs exclusive dining experience Unlimited fine wine, beer and soft drinks with lunch and dinner Unlimited sparkling wine and fresh juice with breakfast Sip & Sail Cocktail Hour with complimentary wine, beer, spirits and soft drinks Tapas, sandwiches, snacks and refreshments served daily in the Main Lounge A WORLD OF EXPLORATION Immersive tours in every destination Gentle, regular, active and late-riser tour options Bike tours and hikes Special interest tours Knowledgeable guides Personal headset for easy exploration Airport transfers with purchase of air from AmaWaterways Book Now

name: Balloon Fiesta & Pueblo Cultural Tour
positioning: In addition to the stunning display that is the Albuquerque Balloon Fiesta, this six-day tour explores the unique history and culture of New Mexico.
overview: Experience the ultimate New Mexico vacation with this premier six-day tour, centered around the world-famous Albuquerque International Balloon Fiesta. After witnessing the breathtaking magic of the festival, your journey continues into the heart of the Land of Enchantment. positioning: Discover Colorado's national parks with an 8-day guided tour. Visit Rocky Mountain, Mesa Verde, Great Sand Dunes, and more. Book your Colorado adventure!

Starting in the metropolitan areas of Denver and Colorado Springs, this tour travels through the Rocky Mountains and San Juan Mountains, where you’ll explore this area through a myriad of activities. Enjoy a visit atop Pikes Peak and other attractions near Colorado Springs. Travel back to your youth with the opportunity to slide down gigantic sand dunes in Great Sand Dunes National Park. positioning: Explore Maui & Hawaiʻi Island on a 10-day guided adventure featuring volcanoes, waterfalls, snorkeling, luau, and stargazing from Maunakea. Small group. Big memories.
overview: Volcanoes, Waterfalls, Reefs, Stars, and 10 days in Paradise Experience the magic of two extraordinary Hawaiian Islands in one unforgettable journey. name: Oregon South Tour
positioning: Explore beautiful parks and monuments like Newberry Volcano National Monument and Crater Lake National Park when you take the Oregon South Tour.
overview: Making a big loop through the western half of Oregon, this tour explores Oregon’s beautiful coastline and its rugged interior, including Crater Lake and other Cascade Mountain points of interest. You’ll experience a thrilling jetboat ride up the Rouge River, see an assortment of both coastal and mountain wildlife, pass through volcanic landscapes, and sample some great fresh food.
itinerary_raw: Day 1: Arrive Portland, Travel to Newport Our tour guide will meet guests at the airport arrivals pick-up area. Please arrive any time prior to 12:00 pm. From there you will travel two hours through the Willamette valley and onto the Pacific Ocean. You will pass through Lincoln City and Depoe Bay on our way to Newport. En route, you will explore the Boiler Bay Overlook and have the opportunity to see this unique ecological area and watch for wildlife and other activity in and around the water. This evening, we will enjoy a fantastic farm-to-table experience at a local restaurant for our tour's welcome dinner. What a great experience to have the joy of eating fresh fish right off the boat. The restaurants here are fantastic, and this will be a treat. Once finished, you can enjoy walking along the beach as the waves crash and the sun sets below the horizon! Lodging: Hallmark Resort, Newport, OR Meals: D Day 2: Newport Area Begin your morning exploring various viewpoints, especially the Yaquina Head Lighthouse and Marine Gardens, just north of Newport. You will also get to enjoy a 2-hour Whale Watching tour with Dockside Depoe Bay. The same whales return year after year and we can identify them by their individual markings. The skippers even name them. Humpback Blues whales are also seen occasionally, though not as frequently as Gray Whales. We are fortunate here in Depoe Bay to have whales nearby for us to see for most of the year. Afterwards, you will have the afternoon to relax and enjoy the Pacific Ocean and the town of Newport Lodging: Hallmark Resort, Newport, OR Meals: B, L Day 3: Newport – Classic Oregon Coastline – Gold Beach Today you will continue south along Oregon’s beautiful coast. Some of the areas you will visit are Heceta Head Lighthouse, Sea Lion Caves, Devil’s Churn, Thor’s Wells, Captain Cook Point, Cape Blanco, and many others. The evening will be in Gold Beach, OR where you can spend your evening relaxing watching the waves or enjoying a walk along the beach to the Rogue River or Turtle Rock Creek. Each room has its own balcony to sit back and enjoy the view! Lodging: SureStay Plus Hotel by Best Western, Gold Beach, OR Meals: B, D Day 4: Gold Beach – Rouge River – Crescent City Be ready this morning for more fun on the water – but this time it’s the Rogue River. This thrilling 64-mile mail-run on a Hydro-jet Boat takes you through shallow riffles and beneath the sheer 400-foot walls of Copper Canyon. As you travel deeper into the federally designated Wild & Scenic River, make sure to have your camera ready to capture osprey, otter, deer and bear, as your professional guide shares the folklore, history, trees, and wildflowers of the area. Your adventure includes a fantastic lunch on an open deck overlooking the river or seated inside with views of the area. The afternoon will find you winding your way down the last part of the Oregon Coast and into Crescent City, California for the night. Lodging: Best Western Plus Northwoods Inn, Crescent City, CA Meals: B, L Day 5: Crescent City – Redwoods – Shady Cove This morning you will have the opportunity to explore Redwood Forests of the Pacific Northwest. These include Prairie Creek Redwoods State Park, Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park, and Jedediah Smith Redwood Grove, one of the best in the state. Also, you will explore the mouth of the Klamath River into the Pacific Ocean, with the opportunity to see sea lions fishing and playing! Once finished, you will then leave the coastal area and head inland, crossing back into Oregon. You will end the day in the quaint town of Shady Cove. Lodging: Edgewater Inn Shady Cove, OR Meals: B, L Day 6: Crater Lake – Bend Today’s travels take you north along Hwy 97 to Crater Lake National Park. Crater Lake is widely known for its amazing depth, intense blue color, pure water, and spectacular views. The Visitor Center can provide valuable information about the lake's history and formation. you will enjoy views of the lake as you hike up to Garfield Peak. After lunch at the Crater Lake Dining Room, you will continue around the lake on a tour of the Rim. This two-hour drive around the lake offers awesome views and stops with plenty of opportunities for picture taking. Also, there will be a few great optional hikes up to The Watchman for more views of the lake and the surrounding areas. Once you've said goodbye to Crater Lake, you'll make your way to Bend. You'll have some time to get acquainted with Central Oregon's biggest city before settling in for the night. Lodging: The Newberry, Bend, OR Meals: B, L Day 7: Journey Back to Portland After breakfast, you will head just south of town and have some adventure at the Newberry Volcano National Monument to see an active volcanic area. Some great hikes are available. Afterwards, you will head north to Portland. Along the way, you will travel past Mount Hood, with views of the glacier up through the Columbia River Gorge. Enjoy the breathtaking views and photo ops of this protected National Scenic Area. You will stop at Multnomah Falls, the second-tallest year-round waterfall in the nation. The water drops 620 feet from its origin on Larch Mountain. You will have a farewell lunch at Multnomah Falls Lodge overlooking the Columbia River. We will arrive at the Portland Airport in the late afternoon. Meals: B, L

You’ll dine at classic Route 66 restaurants, visit historic motels and museums, and meet the people who continue to preserve the legacy of America’s Main Street.

name: Yosemite Half Dome Backpacking Trip: Cathedral Lakes
positioning: Experience a 6-day Yosemite backpacking trip with a Half Dome summit. Guided thru-hike from the High Sierra to Yosemite Valley.
overview: 6-Day Guided Thru-Hike Take on one of the most iconic wilderness journeys in California with this 6-day guided Yosemite backpacking trip featuring a Half Dome summit attempt. Designed as a true thru-hike from the High Sierra to Yosemite Valley, this adventure combines high-alpine scenery, remote backcountry camps, and one of the most sought-after summit experiences in the National Park system. Starting in Yosemite Valley and climbing into the rugged High Country, you’ll traverse dramatic elevation changes—from nearly 11,000 feet down to 4,000 feet—while hiking through granite basins, alpine meadows, and forested trails. With expert guides handling logistics, permits, and instruction, this trip is perfect for adventurous hikers ready to experience Yosemite beyond the crowds.
highlights_raw: Backpack through Yosemite National Park and summit iconic Half Dome Follow expert guides who pass on local knowledge and outdoor skills Take in scenic vistas, glacially-carved features, and magnificent forests Inclusions: All Meals (Breakfast, Lunch, & Dinner) Campsite and Permit Fees Experienced hiking guide with extensive wilderness expertise, medical certifications, and a deep passion for leading adventurers through stunning landscapes. Gear We Provide Trekking Poles Cooking Stove and Cookware Company-issued first-aid Kit Emergency Communication Device(s) Day 1: Yosemite Valley Arrival & Pre-Trip Preparation Your adventure begins in the heart of Yosemite Valley at North Pines Backpackers Camp, where we set the foundation for a successful and rewarding backcountry experience. Our team arrives earlier in the day to prepare camp and ensure everything is ready for your arrival, including securing wilderness permits from the ranger station and organizing group gear. Guests arrive in the afternoon and are welcomed with introductions and a comprehensive orientation led by your expert guides. This is where the trip truly begins—reviewing the route, discussing expectations, and walking through essential backpacking skills. You’ll participate in a hands-on pack fitting and gear demo, learning how to properly distribute weight and efficiently organize your backpack for the days ahead. As you settle into camp, we strongly encourage consistent hydration to help your body adjust in preparation for higher elevations in the coming days. The evening wraps up with a relaxed group dinner in camp, giving everyone a chance to connect, ask questions, and get excited for the journey ahead. Surrounded by Yosemite’s iconic granite walls and towering pines, it’s the perfect introduction to your guided backpacking adventure. Day 2: Cathedral Lakes Trailhead to Upper Cathedral Lake Camp Day two marks the true start of your Yosemite backcountry journey as we head into the High Sierra. The morning begins early with breakfast and final preparations before boarding the hiker shuttle from Curry Village. Enjoy a scenic ride up Tioga Road as we climb toward the trailhead, gaining elevation and leaving the busy valley behind. By late morning, we begin hiking from Cathedral Lakes Trailhead, following a stunning section of the iconic John Muir Trail. Today’s trek covers approximately 5.5 miles with significant elevation gain, making it one of the more physically demanding days of the trip. With full packs and higher altitude, the pace is intentionally steady, allowing time for rest breaks, hydration, and acclimatization. Your guides will closely monitor the group and provide support, coaching, and encouragement throughout the climb. The trail winds through alpine forest and granite landscapes, gradually opening up to expansive High Sierra views. Lunch is flexible and may be enjoyed along the trail or upon arrival near camp, depending on the group’s pace and preference. By late afternoon, we arrive at Upper Cathedral Lake, one of Yosemite’s most iconic alpine settings. Surrounded by towering peaks and pristine wilderness, we’ll set up camp and settle in for the evening. After a well-earned dinner, take time to relax by the lake, soak in the scenery, and enjoy your first night deep in the Yosemite backcountry. Hiking: 5.5 Miles +1500ft/-500ft Day 3: Upper Cathedral Lake to Sunrise & Henry Lake Camp Wake up to a crisp High Sierra morning as your guides prepare breakfast and begin breaking down camp. Mornings at elevation can be cold, and depending on conditions, we may take a bit of extra time to warm up and get moving comfortably before hitting the trail. Today’s route takes us deeper into Yosemite’s high country, covering approximately 7.5 miles as we traverse a dynamic landscape of alpine meadows, granite ridgelines, and forested trails. The day includes both climbs and descents, with a steady rhythm that allows for breaks, hydration, and time to take in the expansive scenery. As always, your guides will set a manageable pace and provide support throughout the hike. Along the way, we pass through the Sunrise area, a beautiful and remote հատված of the park, before continuing toward our destination near Henry Lake. The trail gradually descends into a quieter, less-traveled section of the backcountry, offering a true sense of solitude. By late afternoon, we arrive at camp and get everyone settled in for the evening. After setting up tents and relaxing from the day’s effort, we gather for a well-earned dinner in camp. As the sun sets over the High Sierra, enjoy the peaceful surroundings and the rewarding feeling of another incredible day on the trail. Hiking: 7.5 Miles +1200ft/-1800ft elevation Day 4: Henry Lake to Sunrise Creek via Clouds Rest Day four delivers one of the most unforgettable—and rewarding—experiences of the entire journey. After an early breakfast and packing up camp, we begin our hike toward Sunrise Creek, with the option to summit the iconic Clouds Rest along the way. The day’s route covers approximately 6.5 miles, featuring a mix of steady climbs and descents through classic High Sierra terrain. As we approach Clouds Rest, your guides will prepare the group for what lies ahead. The summit ridge is narrow and exposed, offering breathtaking 360-degree views of Yosemite, including a direct vantage point of Half Dome. For many, this is a highlight of the trip—but it’s important to note that it involves exposure and requires comfort with heights. For guests who prefer a less exposed option or if weather conditions are unfavorable, an alternate route allows us to safely bypass the summit while still continuing toward camp. Your guides will help each guest make the best decision based on comfort level and conditions. After taking in the views and completing the day’s hike, we descend toward Sunrise Creek, where we arrive in the late afternoon. Camp is set among peaceful forest surroundings near flowing water—an ideal place to unwind after a big day on the trail. We wrap up the evening with a well-earned dinner, sharing stories and reflecting on one of Yosemite’s most iconic alpine experiences. Hiking: 6.5 Miles +1000ft/-1800ft elevation Day 5: Half Dome Summit Today is the pinnacle of your Yosemite backpacking adventure—the opportunity to summit the iconic Half Dome. For those aiming to reach the summit at sunrise, the day begins early, waking approximately three hours before first light to begin the ascent under headlamp. This timing offers a quieter, more serene experience and the chance to watch the sun rise over the Sierra from one of the most well-known viewpoints in the park. For others, a more relaxed morning allows for a later start, with flexibility to attempt the summit at a comfortable pace or even in the evening for a sunset experience. The hike to Half Dome is short but demanding, covering 2.7 miles one way with significant elevation gain. The final ascent includes the famous cable route, where your guides provide support, instruction, and encouragement to help you safely reach the top. Summit timing can vary widely depending on group pace and conditions, but reaching the top rewards you with sweeping panoramic views of Yosemite Valley, the High Sierra, and the journey you’ve completed so far. After returning to camp, enjoy a well-deserved lunch and a slower-paced afternoon. Spend time relaxing near Sunrise Creek or along the Merced River, reflecting on the accomplishment and taking in the peaceful surroundings. The evening concludes with dinner in camp, celebrating an unforgettable day in one of Yosemite’s most iconic landscapes. Hiking: 2.7 Miles +2000ft elevation Day 6: Sunrise Creek to Curry Village & Departure Your final day on the trail begins with an early breakfast as your guides break down camp and prepare for the hike out of the backcountry. With packs loaded one last time, we set off toward Curry Village, retracing a scenic route that gradually transitions from remote wilderness back into Yosemite Valley. Today’s hike covers approximately 7.5 miles, featuring a significant descent as we make our way down toward the valley floor. Along the way, enjoy changing perspectives of Yosemite’s iconic landscapes—from quiet forested sections to dramatic granite walls and glimpses of the Merced River below. It’s a rewarding final stretch that offers time to reflect on the journey and everything you’ve accomplished over the past several days. By early to mid-afternoon, we arrive back at Curry Village, marking the completion of your guided backpacking adventure. After de-rigging gear and sharing final moments with your group, we wrap up with goodbyes—leaving you with lasting memories of Yosemite’s backcountry and a true sense of accomplishment. Hiking: 7.5 Miles +1300ft/-4800ft elevation What to Pack: Required Gear Base Layers, Tops, and Bottoms Fleece/Wool Gloves Fleece/Wool Hat Long Sleeve Shirts (Synthetic, Lightweight) Hiking Pants (Quick-Dry, Lightweight) Hiking Socks (Synthetic or Wool) Hiking Boots Casual Shoes for Travel and Free Time Insulated jacket and/or Vest Rain Jacket (Hooded, Lightweight, Waterproof, Breathable) Day Pack (36L-50L) Water Bottles (Three 1-liter) or Hydration System, Plus One 1-liter Water Bottle Personal Bathroom Kit: Toilet Paper, Ziplock Bags, Personal Wipes, Hand Cleaner Prescription Medications Whistle Recommended Gear Bandana or Buff for Sun Protection Hiking Shorts (Quick-Dry, Lightweight) Rain Pants (Lightweight, Waterproof, Breathable) Underwear Sun Hat T-shirts (Cotton and Synthetic) Sunblock and Lip Balm Sunglasses and Accessories Water Shoes (Full Foot Protection) Electrolyte Drink Additives Hand Sanitizer Large Plastic Garbage Bag Pack Rain Cover Toiletries Earplugs You Might Also Consider Camera and Accessories Insect Repellent Liner Socks (Synthetic) Reading and Writing Materials Small Binoculars Face Mask Energy Snacks and Drink Mixes Trail Conditions: This trip follows a mix of well-maintained and more rugged sections of the trail. Be prepared for periods of steep hiking, moderate to significant exposure, and, at times, loose surfaces that require attention and careful footing. Physical Demands of this Trip This trip is rated Vigorous. Participants will carry their own backpack weighing 35 to 40 lbs at a high elevation for several miles over steep, exposed, and rocky terrain, with constant and dramatic elevation gain and/or loss exceeding 2,000' or more per day on most days of this trip. Keep the high elevation of this trip in mind when training for this adventure, as backpacking/hiking will feel harder and use more energy than at lower elevations, especially if coming from a lower elevation/sea level. Previous backpacking experience is highly recommended; this is not a beginner's backpacking trip. To maximize your enjoyment of the trip, we strongly encourage you to be involved in a consistent training regimen starting at least 3-6 months before the trip, ideally including training hikes with a weighted pack. We also recommend staying hydrated before departure to help mitigate the effects of hiking at high altitudes. Your overall fitness level is crucial to your enjoyment of this trip. positioning: Embark on a 12-day Grand Circle tour, exploring iconic national parks like Zion, Grand Canyon, and Arches. Enjoy scenic views, hikes, and local adventures!
overview: Prepare to be swept away on an unforgettable journey through the legendary landscapes of America’s Southwest. The Grand Circle Experience brings you face-to-face with the very best this region has to offer — from the crimson canyons of Zion and the vast expanse of the Grand Canyon to the sculpted arches, winding rivers, and sun-drenched deserts that define the spirit of the West. Every turn reveals a new wonder, every horizon a masterpiece carved by time. Discover the magic of the desert as you explore seven national parks and an array of hidden gems — including Vermilion Cliffs National Monument, Antelope Canyon, and the Grand Staircase–Escalante Monument. Cruise the Colorado River, marvel at Monument Valley’s towering buttes, and journey by rail on the legendary Durango & Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroad. Along the way, experience charming towns like Moab, Durango, and Ouray, and travel the scenic Million Dollar Highway and Highway 12 – All-American Road, two of the most beautiful drives in the country. Guided by local experts who know these lands intimately, you’ll uncover the stories, culture, and landscapes that make the Southwest so unforgettable. From sunrise hikes and panoramic viewpoints to local dining and cultural encounters, every day brings a new adventure. The Grand Circle Experience is more than a tour — it’s a once-in-a-lifetime journey through the heart of the American Southwest.

Up you go, up to the North Rim of the Grand Canyon National Park and visit viewpoints around the North Rim Lodge, including Bright Angel Point and other areas. After lunch, you will continue your journey to Page, Arizona, by crossing the Navajo Bridge spanning the Colorado River, passing by the enormous Vermilion Cliffs, named for their brilliantly crimson striations of sedimentary rock. There will also be a stop at the Navajo Bridge and the Colorado River. Our lodging for the next two nights is near the shores of Lake Powell. Lodging: Courtyard by Marriott Page at Lake Powell​, Page, AZ Meals: B, L Day 4: Colorado River Cruise & Antelope Canyon This half-day adventure is the best way to experience the peaceful grandeur of the Colorado River. Glide through clam, scenic waters with stops at the river's most breathtaking sites. Perfect for all ages and skill levels, this 10-mile journey blends tranquility, natural beauty, and inspiration to create an unforgettable experience. Once finished on water, experience the undulating sandstone-sculpted walls of Antelope Canyon. The lighting and beautiful flow of the walls make this an experience to remember. This will be the highlight of the afternoon! End the afternoon with a view of Horseshoe Bend. Enjoy the evening at the Red Heritage Experience in Page, Arizona. Red Heritage is a Native American Dinner Theater in Page, Arizona, showcasing local dancers talented in colorful powwow dancing, flute playing, and live drum music. You will have an evening of culturally inspired food and an unforgettable show! Lodging: Courtyard by Marriott Page at Lake Powell​, Page, AZ Meals: B, D Day 5: Lake Powell, Monument Valley, and Navajo Nation Today you will head to Kayenta, Arizona, for a brief stop before entering Monument Valley in an open-air truck. Admire the gigantic formations up close or towering along the horizon. You'll also visit filming spots for classic Western movies and lesser-frequented outcroppings in the backcountry. After lunch, you will have some time to explore the historic Gouldings Lodge before continuing to Bluff, UT. Stops will be made at Fort Bluff to learn about the region's early inhabitants. Once finished, travel across the backroads of the Navajo Reservation to Four-Corners Monument, where you will stop to shop and snap a shot at the famous spot where the borders of Colorado, New Mexico, Arizona, and Utah all meet. Afterwards, there will be a short drive to Cortez, CO, where you will lodge for the evening. Lodging: Hampton Inn Mesa Verde-Cortez, CO Meals: B, L Day 6: Mesa Verde National Park to Durango Start your day with breakfast before you travel to Mesa Verde National Park. Here, you'll explore and experience the dramatic ruins of ancient Pueblo cliff houses, built into shallow caves and under rock overhangs. You will also stop at viewpoints and a museum along the mesa top before heading to Durango in the San Juan Mountains. this frontier town offers plent of restaurants and shopping - just the place to enjoy your free evening. Lodging: Holiday Inn & Suites, Durango, CO Meals: B, L Day 7: Durango to Moab Score a true frontier experience with a steam engine train ride on the Durango and Silverton Railroad, an impressive track built in 1881 that snakes along the canyons of the Animas River Valley. It'll be lunchtime when you arrive in Silverton, and the Shady Lady, Bent Elbow, and Natalie's -- all former bordello and current restaurants -- will be happy to accommodate you. Then, trek the twisting turns of the Million Dollar Highway, stopping in Ouray for some shopping before the final leg to Moab. (If traveling from March 1 to May 1, the train ride will be only up to Cascade Canyon.) Lodging: Hyatt Place, Moab, UT Meals: B Day 8: Arches National Park Spend the day exploring Arches National Park and its 2,000 natural sandstone arches, up to 50 of which you'll experience firsthand as you hike to the Delicate Arch, Landscape Arch, Devil's Garden, and Courthouse Towers. Returning to the hotel, you'll have the afternoon free before an early dinner at a local restaurant, giving you plenty of time to head over to Dead Horse Point for a beautiful sunset overlooking the Colorado River. Lodging: Hyatt Place, Moab, UT Meals: B, L, D Day 9: Canyonlands to Capitol Reef National Parks Today, you're treated to another scenic drive into Canyonlands National Park to see and experience the majestic Mesa Arch in the morning. This is the best time to photograph this formation. You will then enjoy the San Rafael Swell on the way to Capitol Reef National Park, where you'll hike up to Hickman Bridge, enjoy the Grand Wash, and look for Geodes and other activities within this fantastic park. Dinner and an enjoyable evening will be experienced at one of the local hotels in this area. Lodging: Red Sands or Broken Spur Inn, Torrey, UT Meals: B, L Day 10: Capitol Reef to Bryce Canyon National Parks After a morning exploring Capitol Reef National Park, you will journey down Highway 12, known as the All-American Road for its iconic vistas, and also the deep canyons that have been carved through the landscape before arriving at Bryce Canyon National Park, a Utah treasure filled with unearthly archways and rose-colored hoodoos. You'll spend the evening hiking the stunning canyon, relaxing, and dining on your own in Bryce Canyon. This evening, you will have the option to enjoy the stars and the area's solitude. Exploring the wonders of the universe on this Bryce Canyon Stargazing Tour, led by expert guides eager to share the mysteries of the night sky. Lodging: Best Western Plus Bryce Canyon Grand Hotel, Bryce Canyon, UT Meals: B, L Day 11: Bryce Canyon to Las Vegas Your last day in the Southwest's fantastic landscape starts with a stellar sendoff of early morning sun lighting up pink cliffs during an unforgettable sunrise in Bryce Canyon. After hiking and exploring more of the canyon, you'll head back to Las Vegas, stopping for a few final views of Zion National Park from the Kolob Canyons and lunch at a local joint in Cedar City, Utah. After lunch begin your return drive to Las Vegas through the historic town of St George, UT. Hotel drop off by 6:00 pm PST. Thank you for traveling with us! Lodging: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Las Vegas Airport Meals: B, L Day 12: Travel Home Transfer to the Las Vegas Airport by hotel shuttle on your own for your departure flight home. Meals: B

Peaks that soar to 14,000 feet, broad valleys teeming with wildlife, glaciers, thermal features, and barren landscapes still recovering from the ravages of volcanic eruptions and forest fires are awaiting you. Spend eight exciting days exploring and learning about the unique geological and ecological history that continues to shape this region, how it came into existence, and about the plants and animals that call this wilderness home. Your adventure awaits! Contact us to book today! name: Glacier National Park Tour
positioning: Discover the unforgettable beauty of Glacier National Park and take a tour of Sierra Silver Mine and cruise on Saint Mary Lake. Contact us today to learn more!
overview: See the grandeur of Glacier National Park – “The Crown of the Continent”. Beginning and ending in Missoula, this tour visits sites such as the National Bison Range, Flathead Lake, as well as spending six magical days in Glacier National Park. A tour through this region of Montana and the Rocky Mountains is a genuine treat to anyone with a sense of adventure and a love for the wild. The scenery you will see was carved long ago by glaciation and massive floods from glacial lake outbursts. When you take an intimate small group tour with us through this ultra-scenic area, you’ll learn firsthand why it’s referred to as “Big Sky Country”. Our Glacier National Park tours in Montana will take you through panoramic views and quaint towns, and also offer opportunities for wildlife viewing. The park is home to over 70 species of mammals, including grizzly bears, wolves, elk, and mountain goats. In addition to the diverse wildlife, Glacier National Park boasts more than a million acres of pristine wilderness. With over 700 lakes and hundreds of miles of hiking trails, there are endless opportunities for outdoor recreation. Visitors can go camping, fishing, horseback riding, boating, or simply take in the stunning scenery from one of the many viewpoints. Enjoy the comfort and convenience of our guided tours, where we take care of all the planning and logistics so you can focus on making unforgettable memories. Our knowledgeable Glacier National Park tour guides will provide insight into the area's history, geology, and wildlife, making your trip more enriching.
itinerary_raw: Day 1: Arrive Missoula Montana Fly into Missoula, MT, any time today. Upon arrival, you will be transferred to the hotel via the hotel shuttle. Your Southwest Adventure Tours guide will meet you in the lobby with your room key and get you situated and ready for your adventure. You will get to meet the rest of your tour group and enjoy a welcome dinner together at 7:00pm Lodging: BW Plus Grant Creek Inn, Missoula, MT Meals: D Day 2: National Bison Range, Big Fork, Glacier National Park Travel north through “Big Sky Country” and start your day with a visit to the National Bison Range. Afterwards, enjoy a scenic drive along the shores of Flathead Lake on your way to the small lakeside town of Big Fork. Big Fork is home to wonderful art galleries and restaurants. You will have time to explore and have lunch on your own. In the afternoon, you will continue traveling through Glacier National Park, over to the east side of the park and explore Two Medicine Lake, Running Eagle Falls, Appistaki Falls, and other areas. End your day relaxing at your lodging. Lodging: Mountain Pine Motel, East Glacier Park, MT Meals: B, D Day 3: Glacier National Park to East Glacier Today, you will take in the grandeur of Glacier National Park "The Crown of the Continent,” as you begin with a scenic drive through the area, passing by St Mary’s to Many Glacier. We will have the full day available to explore the Many Glacier section of the park. You can choose to spend your with options of hiking, horseback riding, kayaking, canoeing, or relaxing on the shores of Swiftcurrent Lake or Lake Josephine. In the late afternoon, you will have the opportunity to enjoy a unique experience with Iron Shield Creative. This experience includes a cultural adventure hike with an Indigenous team and an opportunity to learn about the ancient stories and history of Glacier National Park. This is a special experience you won't soon forget! Once finished, you will return to your hotel and then have a group dinner at a local restaurant. Lodging: Mountain Pine Motel, East Glacier Park, MT Meals: B, L Day 4: Glacier National Park, Boat Tour, Going to the Sun Road After checking out of the hotel, you will travel to St Mary’s. The morning will be spent exploring this area including a scenic cruise on St Mary’s and a short hike to a waterfall. After lunch, you will travel the world famous Going to the Sun Road from St Mary’s to Lake McDonald. Take a 52-mile drive that crests the Continental Divide at Logan Pass, famous for its majestic snow-capped mountains, deep valleys, and shimmering lakes. In the late afternoon, you will travel to Whitefish and your hotel, with evening free to explore the downtown area of Whitefish. After breakfast, depart the hotel for a visit to Lake McDonald, where you'll have to opportunity to hike, paddle by kayak or canoe, or simply relax along the peaceful shores near Apgar. Afterward, continue to Polebridge for lunch at the historic Northern Lights Sallon and take the time to explore this rustic, off-the-grid community. Advanced reservations are recommended) Lodging: BW Rocky Mountain Lodge, Whitefish, MT Meals: B, L Day 6: Glacier National Park, Rafting the Flathead River Finish off your Glacier National Park experience by Rafting on the Middle Fork of the Flathead River. Meals: B

itinerary_raw: Day 1: Canyonlands & Arches National Park Today you will explore the two National Parks outside Moab – Canyonlands & Arches National Park! Canyonlands is known for its districts, Canyonlands includes rugged land, canyons and plateaus carved by two rivers: The Colorado and the Green. The most popular place to visit is the Island in the Sky District which is a sheer walled mesa in the Northern part of the park. It has some of the most popular viewpoints including Grand View Arch, Mesa Arch, and Green River Overlook. You will see some fantastic views on this tour! You will have a stop for lunch before heading to Arches. Known for its over 2000 naturally created sandstone arches, Arches is full of amazing hikes, scenic views and much more! You will have a chance to explore Arches through hiking and a scenic drive. You can choose from the following: Delicate Arch, Landscape Arch, Windows Sections, (all time permitting). Please note that it takes approximately 4-4.5 hours each way from Salt Lake City. The tour lasts approximately 12-14 hours.

name: Arizona Bird Watching and Tucson Adventure
overview: Home View Our Tours Arizona Bird Watching and Tucson Adventure Cochise County is one of America's most scenic places and offers the perfect opportunity to see all the winter migrants that travel into and through Southeastern Arizona. Along with the opportunities for birdwatching, you will have the opportunity to learn about photography, geology, history, botany, and agriculture in this area and to see the other wildlife and natural wonders of Southeastern Arizona. Along with the wildlife comes over 3000 years of gastronomic history and culture that has developed in this area. Enjoy learning and experiencing this cultural heritage on this 7 day 6 night adventure.
itinerary_raw: DAY 1: Tucson, AZ Today your adventure begins as you arrive at the Tucson Airport by 1:00pm to start your “winter wonderland” tour. (*Please arrive at the Tucson Airport before 1:00pm) You will meet your local guide, then go explore the Pima Air and Space Museum. This is one of the worlds largest non-government funded aerospace museums. It features nearly 350 historical aircraft over 80 acres. You will have the opportunity to learn about this unique destination including the opportunity to enjoy a Docent-led tour of the Aircraft Boneyard. Once finished, you will transfer to your hotel. After checking in and getting unpacked, you will join the group for a welcome dinner at one of the many unique restaurants found in Tucson. Lodging – Embassy Suites, Tucson, AZ Meals: D DAY 2: Sonoran Desert – Old Tucson-Mission San Xavier This morning you will get to wander through Saguaro National Park and the Sonoran Desert Museum. You will have a firsthand experience hiking and exploring this unique landscape and learn about the fragile ecosystem that survives in this extreme environment. Afterwards you will get to visit Old Tucson Movie Studios and Adventure Park for lunch and a step back in time. Built in 1939 by Columbia Pictures, this area has been used in multiple movies and gives you see the Wild West. Once finished you will travel south to Mission San Xavier del Bac and roam around this unique and historical Spanish Catholic Mission. Built originally in 1797, this mission is a small piece of the architectural and cultural history of this area. Upon finishing this, you will enjoy a tour/dinner in Tucson. Named a UNESCO Gastronomy Heritage City, you will get to taste some of the cuisines that has been in existence for over 3000 years. Lodging – Embassy Suites, Tucson, AZ Meals: B, D DAY 3: Kartchner Caverns – Tombstone - Wilcox Enjoy a beautiful winter day with incredible views of Tucson as you travel south to Kartchner Caverns. You will explore this unique cave system. Discovered in 1974 and protected until it was created as a state park in 1988, this cave has beautiful features that will be a joy to see. Along with that, you will get to enjoy exploring other areas of the park including the Hummingbird Garden. Once finished you will travel to Tombstone, AZ for another experience in the history of the West. You can enjoy a visit to the OK Corral and other unique areas of Historic Allen Street, along with Boothill Cemetery and the Historic Courthouse. Dinner will be at one of the fine local historical establishments in Tombstone. Then we will travel north to Wilcox, AZ where you will be based for the rest of the week. Lodging – Holiday Inn Express, Wilcox, AZ Meals: B, D DAY 4: Birdwatching in Wilcox Cochise County is one of America's most scenic places and offers the perfect opportunity to see all the winter migrants that travel into and through Southeastern Arizona. Along with the opportunities for birdwatching, you will learn about photography, geology, history, botany, and agriculture in this area and to see the other wildlife and natural wonders of Southeastern Arizona. This morning you will start with birding at Indian Bread Rocks Recreation Area and Dos Cabezas. After a late lunch you will have time to relax before heading out for an evening of sighting Sandhill Cranes and other fowl. Lodging – Holiday Inn Express, Wilcox, AZ Meals: B, L DAY 5: Birdwatching in Wilcox This morning you will spend your time birdwatching in the Chirichaua Mountains. This is one of the best places in Southern Arizona for birding with over 300+ species documented to be in the area. With elevations ranging from 4000 to 9700 ft above sea level, there are multiple plant communities able to support a wide variety of birds. It is also the northern most range for many species found in Mexico. In the late afternoon you will travel south and enjoy more birdwatching at Whitewater Draw. This area has droves of Sandhill Cranes and other waterfowl that call this place home for the winter. With the Dragoon Mountains in the background, this area offers fantastic photographic opportunities. It is one of the many hidden gems of Southwest Arizona. Lodging – Holiday Inn Express, Wilcox, AZ Meals: B, L DAY 6: Birdwatching in Wilcox This morning will start with sunrise photographing Sandhill Cranes. Afterwards you will enjoy a Hawk Stalk northward towards Safford, AZ. After lunch, enjoy birdwatching at Roper Lake and Dankworth Pond. Along with multiple species frequenting these areas you may also see bobcats, raccoons, and coyotes. You will finish the evening with the opportunity for a final Sunset with the Sandhill Cranes. Lodging – Holiday Inn Express, Wilcox, AZ Meals: B, L, D DAY 7: Journey Home This morning, transfer to the Tucson Airport for your return flight home. Meals: B

name: Magnificent Alaska!
overview: Alaska, the last frontier. Join us with the opportunity to experience the vast expanse of wilderness by sea, land, rail, and air. Explore its immense regions and view its diverse wildlife. Come along and spend 10 days with an intimate group of 10 adventure seekers traversing this land of enchantment. Our Magnificent Alaska tour begins and ends in Anchorage and takes you south to the Kenai Peninsula, including stays in the towns of Homer and Seward, where you'll see classic Alaska scenery. While in Homer, you'll be taken by seaplane over the Cook Inlet to Katmai National Park for grizzly bear watching. While in Seward, you'll embark on a 6-hour ocean cruise through Kenai Fjords National Park with its stunningly scenic and rugged coastline, numerous tidewater glaciers, and abundant wildlife. Then our tour heads inland to the Denali area, taking in a jet boat tour, a land tour into the interior of Denali National Park, and a flight over North America's tallest Peak, Denali.
itinerary_raw: Day 1: Arrive Anchorage Arrive at Anchorage and check into hotel. Tour historic downtown Anchorage with your guide. This fully narrated trip visits cultural and historical sites including Lake Hood, scenic viewpoints, and Earthquake Park. Group dinner to celebrate the start of our Alaskan adventure (included). Lodging: Springhill Suites Midtown, Anchorage, AK Meals: D Day 2: Anchorage to Homer Drive along the Turnagain Arm of Cook Inlet, home to one of the largest bore tides (it forms a wave) in the world, looking for Beluga Whales. We will visit the Wildlife Conservation Center. The center’s mission is to provide refuge for orphaned, injured, and ill animals. The road to Homer is one of the most scenic drives in Alaska! There will be many stops along the way for scenic viewing and points of interest. Total drive time 4.5 hours. Lodging: Best Western Bidarka Inn, Homer, AK Meals: B, L Day 3: Homer / Katmai National Park or Lake Clark National Park Fly from Homer to Katmai National Park or Lake Clark National Park (based on weather) to see Grizzly Bears. We will catch a glimpse of the bears as we hike about 4-5 miles over 3 hours through braided rivers and meadows to see them in their natural habitat. In the late afternoon we will visit the Alaska Islands and Oceans Visitor Center (If Open). Lodging: Best Western Bidarka Inn, Homer, AK Meals: B, L Day 4: Homer/Hiking Kachemak Bay/Seward/Exit Glacier This morning, enjoy one of the best hikes in the area. Begin with a water taxi from Homer to Kachemak Bay State Park. After your drop off at the Glacier Spit, begin your hike through the forests of Alaska. For the first 1.5 miles, the trail meanders through mixed cottonwood and Sitka spruce. These cottonwoods are some of the largest in the park so take time to appreciate their enormous size. After 1.5 miles, the trail proceeds straight towards the lake on alluvial flats. Keep an eye out for small hawks and bald eagles hunting from treetops in this area. Enjoy a breathtaking view of Grewingk Glacier, a glacier lake full of icebergs and the seclusion of the Alaska wilderness before finishing your hike out the Saddle Trail. Return to Homer on the water taxi for your final view of this timeless landscape. After lunch you will traverse the peninsula as you travel into Seward, AK. We will drive the scenic road to the picturesque city of Seward. Total drive time 4.5 hrs. After checking into your hotel and an early dinner you will end the day exploring Exit Glacier and Kenai Fjords National Park. Multiple hikes and scenic walks are available to choose this evening as you enjoy the sun setting in this iconic wilderness. Don’t miss this day full of adventure! Lodging: Harbor 360 Hotel, Seward, AK Meals: B, L Day 5: Seward – Sea Kayaking, Optional Helicopter Flight & Dog Sledding, Hiking We will start the day by sea kayaking along the dramatic coastline of Resurrection Bay. This trip will be a perfect introduction to sea kayaking and a great opportunity to take in the towering mountains, soaring bald eagles, curious harbor seals, and an enchanting ghost forest. After lunch in town, an optional activity today would be a helicopter flight up to a glacier and then dogsled rides on top of the glacier: Take off in one of our helicopters and find yourself landing at dog camp atop an ancient glacier. A team of sled dogs anxiously awaits to pull you across perfect white snow. Dog sled tours on Godwin Glacier are some of the most fun you can have in Alaska! After your sled ride, cuddle the lovable puppies, take pictures of the beautiful Alaskan scenery, and talk with your Alaskan musher about his best trail stories. We have all the gear and equipment you’ll need for your Alaskan dog sledding experience; you just need to bring your camera. This is a 1.5-hour tour that includes 15 minutes of flight seeing and an unforgettable dog sled ride. $615.00 per person. Lodging: Harbor 360 Hotel, Seward, AK Meals: B, L Day 6: Seward – Kenai Fjords – train to Anchorage This morning, we head out for a 8.5-hour nature cruise in Kenai Fjords National Park. You will be watching for puffins, sea otters, humpback whales, sea lions, and cormorants as we go to one of the least visited fjords for an up close and personal view of a tidewater glacier in Northwestern Fjord. These types of glaciers calve directly into the ocean. In the evening you will enjoy dinner on a scenic train ride back to Anchorage on the Coastal Classic Train - Adventure Class service Lodging: Springhill Suites Midtown, Anchorage, AK Meals: B, L, D Day 7: Anchorage to Talkeetna / Denali Flight Seeing Take your time getting up this morning before beginning your exploration of the Glaciers, Mountains, Rivers, and Tundra that Alaska is famously known for. As you leave Anchorage, your first stop will be at the Alaska Native Heritage Center. The Alaska Native Heritage Center offers a unique experience for you to learn and explore the traditional and contemporary ways of Alaska’s Indigenous cultures. More than a museum, the Center is a place to engage and interact–to ask questions and discover. Our living cultures continue to flourish in a changing world, and although our world changes, our values and traditions remain. Your visit today will take you on a journey through 10,000 years of Alaska Native history and culture through art, dance, Native Games demonstrations, exhibits, traditional Native dwellings, films and more. Afterwards, continue to the Matanuska Glacier with a beautiful scenic drive on the Glen Highway. Your next adventure is exploring the Matanuska Glacier with a 2-3 hour ice excursion! Your afternoon will be spent exploring blue and basal ice, as well as learning about the history and glaciology of the Matanuska Valley in Southcentral Alaska. Enjoy a hands-on adventure while having a truly Alaskan experience. The recessional moraine leads to the terminus, where you and your guide will venture into a wondrous world of glacial features, including moulins, crevasses, open water streams, and conduits. This will be an afternoon you won’t soon forget! Lodging: Grand View Inn & Suites, Wasilla, AK Meals: B, L Day 8: Jet Boat Wilderness Adventure / Denali State Park This morning you will experience an Alaska Wilderness Adventure up the Susitna River. Behold the splendor of Denali and the great Alaska Range from a spectacular vantage point on the Susitna River in our technically advanced jet boat! The folklore, artifacts and panoramic views combine to make this unique 20-mile Alaska river adventure unforgettable. Your 2-hour trip begins aboard the fifty-two-passenger "Talkeetna Queen" or one of her 15 or 20-passenger little sister boats, as it whisks you into the heart of the wilderness in comfort. These are the most technologically advanced jet boats in Alaska designed to safely navigate rivers that were previously inaccessible. As you travel twenty miles of river, your naturalist will talk about the history and rivers in the area and information about Denali. You may have opportunities to view bald eagles that nest in the area. Upon arriving at our Adventure site, you will take a ¼-mile leisurely nature walk to a Dena'ina Indian Encampment, which was the earliest native settlement in the area. You will also visit an authentic trapper’s cabin with its original furnishings and view how trappers lived in "bush" Alaska at the turn of the century. Your experienced guide will display furs from the local area and demonstrate trapping methods. Naturalists will also acquaint you with the wildflowers and plants that grow in abundance along the river system and you will learn about the edible plants that were used by the Native Indians for cooking and medicines and some that are still eaten today. This afternoon, we take a flight to see the tallest peak in North America. Fly up to 6 miles (10 km) from Denali's summit, then descend into the awe-inspiring Ruth Amphitheater and Great Gorge. View the Tokositna and Ruth Glaciers, the sharp ridges of Mount Huntington, hanging glaciers clinging to Mount Hunter, the famous Moose's Tooth, as well as the stunning views of the 45-mile-long Kahiltna Glacier. Pass by Little Switzerland and its peaks. View the world-famous Kahiltna Base Camp and the formidable east face of Mount Foraker. Discover for yourself why this is our most popular tour of Denali National Park. Late this afternoon, enjoy exploring north through Alaska with stops at Denali State Park and other areas before arriving in the small town of Denali and your resort for the evening. Enjoy relaxing at your hotel. Nestled on the banks of the Nenana River, you can enjoy multiple walking and hiking options along with wildlife viewing or just relax on the patio of the main Lodge! Lodging: Denali Park Village, Denali Park, AK Meals: B, L Day 9: Denali Tundra Tour Today is your day to explore Denali National Park! The Tundra Wilderness Tour is the premier tour of Denali National Park and Preserve! This tour offers wonderful diversity for visitors. Incredible scenery, a narrated history of the park road, and some of the best opportunities to view the park’s wildlife inhabitants await you on this tour. The Tundra Wilderness Tour will guide you along a spectacular road corridor, promising different experiences every day, as Denali's wildlife moves at its own pace and according to the seasons. During the main summer season, your tour will continue beyond the Toklat rest area to Stony Hill Overlook, which offers awe-inspiring views of the Alaska Range and, if conditions permit, North America's highest peak. A bottle of water and a snack pack are included with this tour. The rest of the day is yours to relax and explore the area. Explore Denali National Park Visitors Center and the small town of Denali. There are some great shorter hikes and walks to enjoy as you explore this beautiful destination. Those interested can take the hiker shuttle into the park with pre-purchased tickets and enjoy some of the longer hikes available inside the park. Or you can return to Denali Park Village and enjoy the afternoon relaxing in the Alaskan Wilderness! Lodging: Denali Park Village, Denali, AK Meals: B, D Day 10: Denali to Anchorage We depart Denali and drive south back to Anchorage, AK. The group will enjoy a farewell lunch. You may schedule your departure flight for 3pm or later. Total drive time 4 hrs. Meals: B, L

name: Grand Teton & Yellowstone Explorer Tour
positioning: Experience the rugged beauty of Grand Teton & Yellowstone with guided tours featuring wildlife, geysers, and scenic landscapes. Embark on your adventure today!
overview: From a land built on fire, earthquakes, and other extreme geological forces, Yellowstone and Grand Teton National Parks are comprised of two unique ecosystems. Peaks that soar to 14,000 feet, broad valleys teeming with wildlife, glaciers, thermal features, and barren landscapes still recovering from the ravages of volcanic eruptions and forest fires are awaiting you. Spend eight exciting days exploring and learning about the unique geological and ecological history that continues to shape this region, how it came into existence, and about the plants and animals that call this wilderness home. Your adventure awaits!
itinerary_raw: Day 1: Welcome to Salt Lake City, UT Welcome to Salt Lake City, Utah (SLC)—the perfect gateway to your Grand Teton and Yellowstone national park tour. Arrive by late afternoon and arrange your own transportation from the airport to your hotel. Take some time to settle in before the adventure begins. This evening, enjoy a welcome dinner with your fellow travelers to discuss the exciting national park journey ahead. Following dinner, you will head to Temple Square to experience the historic 2027 Salt Lake Temple Open House. Following a massive, five-year renovation to add seismic reinforcements and restore the grounds, this highly anticipated event marks the first public open house since 1893. When the original pioneers completed the temple over a century ago, visitors were allowed to tour it just before its dedication—and now, history is repeating itself. Public Open House Dates: April 5, 2027 – October 1, 2027. Historical Significance: The first time the general public has been allowed inside the Salt Lake Temple in 134 years. Lodging: AC Hotel, Salt Lake City, UT Day 2: Salt Lake City to Jackson, WY This morning, your guide will pick you up at the hotel at 7:00 am to depart for Jackson, WY. Learn about the unique geology and history of Northern Utah, Southeastern Idaho and Western Wyoming on the way to Jackson, WY. After a hearty western-style cookout along the Snake River, enjoy a one-of-a-kind, 10-mile scenic float trip. (peak season only) Lodging: Elk Country Inn, Jackson, WY Meals: B, L, D Day 3: Grand Teton National Park Today you will enter Grand Teton National Park and start your day with wildlife viewing and photography opportunities at Schwabacher Landing and Mormon Row. Arrive at Jenny Lake and enjoy a boat ride across before a hike to Hidden Falls and/or Inspiration Point. (The shuttle typically begins operating after May 15th and normally closes in late September, weather and ice conditions permitting.) Next, head north to Jackson Lake and Colter Bay for lunch and an early afternoon of more hiking and wildlife watching. After a few hours of rest and an early dinner, you will return to Grand Teton for an evening of wildlife watching and adventure! Lodging: Elk Country Inn, Jackson, WY Meals: B, L Day 4: Jackson Hole to Gardiner via Yellowstone NP Enjoy a scenic journey into Yellowstone National Park, beginning with the steaming pools of West Thumb Geyser Basin, the serene shores of Jackson Lake, and the wildlife-filled Hayden Valley. Enjoy a relaxing lunch at Canyon Junction before taking in the dramatic vistas and waterfalls of the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone. Your day concludes with a picturesque ride to Gardiner, where you'll be dropped off at your hotel to enjoy a free evening in this charming gateway town. Lodging: Roosevelt Hotel, Gardiner, MT Meals: B, L Day 5: Gardiner to West Yellowstone Begin your day with early wildlife viewing in the famed Lamar Valley before continuing on to the rugged beauty of the Tower Falls and Roosevelt Areas. After a midday break for lunch, explore the striking terraces of Mammoth Hot Springs. Then journey south to take in Gibbon Falls and wander the geothermal wonders of the Norris Geyser Basin. Conclude your adventure with a scenic drive through the Madison River Valley, arriving in West Yellowstone for an evening free to relax and explore this lively western town. Lodging: Kelly Inn or similar, West Yellowstone, MT Meals: B, L Day 6: Yellowstone National Park Today, along with wildlife watching, you will explore the main geothermal areas of Yellowstone NP, the Old Faithful Geyser Basin, and the Old Faithful Lodge. Afterwards, continue your way to Madison Junction with stops at Grand Prismatic Spring overlook, Firehole Geyser Basin, and other areas. There will be some great hikes and multiple opportunities to enjoy watching wildlife within the park. Lodging: Kelly Inn or similar, West Yellowstone, MT Meals: B, L Day 7: West Yellowstone to Salt Lake City This morning will be spent exploring just outside of Yellowstone NP in Island Park, with stops along the way at places such as Big Springs and Mesa Falls. Continue south through the potato fields of Idaho, then along the shore of the Great Salt Lake. You will return to Salt Lake City by 6:00 pm. Lodging: AC Hotel, Salt Lake City, UT Meals: B, L Day 8: Travel Home This morning, if time allows you are free to explore Salt Lake City. When the time comes, you will transfer to the Salt Lake City Airport on your own to catch your flight home. Meals: B

name: Park City & Olympic Heritage Excursion
positioning: Enjoy a tour of the iconic venues of the 2002 Winter Olympic Games in both Salt Lake City and Park City.
overview: Immerse yourself in Utah's captivating Winter Olympic history on this full-day tour! Journey from Salt Lake City to explore the venues that hosted the world's best athletes in 2002. Stand beside the iconic cauldron, a lasting symbol of the games, and envision the excitement of the opening and closing ceremonies held at Rice-Eccles Stadium. Travel to Park City, home to the renowned Utah Olympic Park. Take a fascinating 1.5-hour tour, delving into the park's history and significance in the Games. Ascend to the top of the park for breathtaking panoramic views that will leave you speechless. Embark on a scenic exploration of Park City. Uncover the town's fascinating past, from its mining roots to its transformation into a world-class ski destination. Stroll down the charming pedestrian Main Street, bustling with shops, restaurants, and historic buildings. Savor a delicious lunch on your own and soak in the mountain ambiance. The afternoon winds down with a scenic drive past Deer Valley Resort, another prominent venue of the 2002 Winter Olympics. Relax and unwind on the return journey to Salt Lake City, where you'll be conveniently dropped off at your hotel by approximately 4:30 PM. This tour is perfect for winter sports enthusiasts, history buffs, and anyone seeking a unique and unforgettable Utah experience. Don't miss this opportunity to relive the magic of the 2002 Winter Olympic Game and explore the captivating legacy of Utah's winter sports scene!
